steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rapid boil. Cook egg noodles at a boil until tender yet firm to the bite, 10 to 12 minutes. Drain.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Toss cooked noodles with sour cream, cottage cheese, raisins, 1/2 cup sugar, and eggs until well blended; pour into the prepared baking dish. Dot top with butter pieces.
Combine remaining 1/2 cup sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over noodles.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is lightly brown, about 45 minutes. Remove from oven; cool to set pudding before serving, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Lynn's Easy Noodle Pudding
raw_recipe.description: Lynn's easy noodle pudding recipe (aka kugel) is tossed with cottage cheese, sour cream, eggs, and raisins and topped with a cinnamon-sugar mixture.
raw_recipe.name: Lynn's Easy Noodle Pudding

review.reviewBody: My family has made/eaten kugel for years. All of them hands down said it was the best they have ever had and asked for the recipe. I recommend you make the following 2 modifications: I used 3 eggs instead of 2. Secondly, I used ricotta cheese instead of cottage cheese. If you use the recipe you can't go wrong!

This was such a hit I need to double or triple the recipe next time. 

Used apricots because I didn't have raisins. Pot style cottage cheese because it's more authentic. Mixed cinnamon and butter into mix. Used half the sugar.

This recipe is easy to make. Since some reviewers said it is a bit bland, I added 1 tsp vanilla and 2 Granny Smith apples, peeled and chopped, along with the raisins in the recipe. I also uses 4 eggs instead of just two, for binding reasons. It was a hit! I will make it again.

I have made this recipe many times and it is always a hit. As is, it is great. I also tweak it to meet my family's picky side. They didn't like the raisins. I omit them. I even tried crasians. Nope. I gotta leave them out. I use ricotta instead of Cottage cheese most of the time. One teaspoon of vanilla, as well. Everything else remains the same. If I was the only one eating this I would leave it as is with the exception of the vanilla. Oh, by the way, in my husband's Jewish family they have it with applesauce or a side of raspberry or strawberry preserves. More like dessert than dinner. Thank you for the great recipe.

I misplaced my families favorite Kugel recipe that I have been making for years so I reluctanly tried this recipe. My family loved it and it has now become the new family kugel recipe for the holidays. The only change I made was to use 4 cups of sour cream instead of the cottage cheese and an extra egg. It made it fluffier and lighter.

My children love this sweet noodle kugel! I gave it only 4 stars because I made a bunch of changes - to make it a healthier dinner - I omitted the sour cream and butter, and i left out the raisins (my kids don't like them). I added a third egg to ensure the mixture will hold together - very sweet and delicious! UPDATE: I made this for PASSOVER by substituting matzo farfel for the noodles! I used 1 package of farfel, soaked it in warm water for about i minute, drained it, and then continued using the other healthier substitutions mentioned above.
This was really easy and great tasting. I used prunes instead of raisins, and I think next time I will add 2 more eggs, and use half the butter.
Super easy and delicious! Made it for a potluck and it was a big hit!

Amazing! I made this for someone who never tasted noodle pudding. WOW!
 I listened to another person who reviewed this recipe and added a 3rd egg. Note sure if it changed anything. Yum Yum Yum!
Yes, this is the recipe I was looking for. Sounds EXACTLY like my nana's recipe. Thank you!
Hello! Great and easy and most of all YUMMY. My kids and husband love it.

I made this for Rosh Hashana dinner (also made a parve version) and it was delish! Left out the raisins as my husband doesn't like them but other than that, stuck to the recipe. Guests loved it, I loved it!
Easy to make but rather bland.
This was a yummy and creamy, yet surprisingly light dessert!
This was pretty good, as noodle puddings (kugels) go. I find most of them bland, and this was no exception, but it was pleasantly creamy. Instead of butter I just used a good spritz of PAM.
